title: Bekhorot 14
description: A new mishna sets animals consecrated with a permanent blemish against animals blemished after consecration, and the Gemara works through its rulings: firstborn and gifts, shearing and labor, offspring, slaughter outside, substitutes, and an animal that died before it was redeemed.
topics: ⚖️ Blemish before consecration or after: two sets of rulings
💰 Sanctity of value exempts from the firstborn and the gifts
✂️ Shearing and labor: does the mishna support Rabbi Eliezer?
🐑 Offspring of a blemished consecrated animal: redeemed unblemished? Rava on a male consecrated for its value
🪨 Rabbi Elazar: a blemished animal on a private altar, and five other ways to read “You shall not sacrifice”
🔄 “Good for bad”: only an animal good at the outset makes a substitute
⚰️ If they died: Rabbi Shimon, the school of Levi, and standing and valuation

a1.he: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁקָּדַם מוּם קָבוּעַ לְהֶקְדֵּשָׁן וְנִפְדּוּ — חַיָּיבִין בַּבְּכוֹרָה וּבַמַּתָּנוֹת, וְיוֹצְאִין לְחוּלִּין לִיגָּזֵז וְלֵיעָבֵד, וְלָדָן וַחֲלָבָן מוּתָּר לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן.

a2.he: וְהַשּׁוֹחֲטָן בַּחוּץ פָּטוּר, וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה, וְאִם מֵתוּ — יִפָּדוּ, חוּץ מִן הַבְּכוֹר וּמִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר.

a3.he: וְכׇל שֶׁקָּדַם הֶקְדֵּשָׁן אֶת מוּמָן, אוֹ מוּם עוֹבֵר לְהֶקְדֵּשָׁן, וּלְאַחַר מִכָּאן נוֹלַד לָהֶן מוּם קָבוּעַ לְהֶקְדֵּשָׁן וְנִפְדּוּ — פְּטוּרִין מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה וּמִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת, וְאֵינָן יוֹצְאִין לְחוּלִּין לִיגָּזֵז וְלֵיעָבֵד.

a4.he: וְלָדָן וַחֲלָבָן אָסוּר לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן, וְהַשּׁוֹחֲטָן בַּחוּץ חַיָּיב, וְעוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה, וְאִם מֵתוּ — יִקָּבֵרוּ.

a5.he: גְּמָ׳ טַעְמָא דְּנִפְדּוּ, הָא לֹא נִפְדּוּ — פְּטוּרִין מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה וּמִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת. קָסָבַר: קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים מְדַחָה מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה וּמִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת.

a6.he: וְיוֹצְאִין לְחוּלִּין וְכוּ׳. טַעְמָא דְּנִפְדּוּ, הָא לֹא נִפְדּוּ — אֲסִירִי בְּגִיזָּה וַעֲבוֹדָה. מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, דְּאָמַר: קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת אֲסוּרִין בְּגִיזָּה וַעֲבוֹדָה?

a7.he: אָמְרִי: לָא, קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים לַמִּזְבֵּחַ הוּא דְּמִיחַלְּפָא בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף לַמִּזְבֵּחַ, גְּזַרוּ בְּהוּ רַבָּנַן, אֲבָל קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת — לָא.

a8.he: וְלָדָן וַחֲלָבָן מוּתָּר כּוּ׳. הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא דְּאִיעַבַּר וְאִתְיְלִיד לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן — פְּשִׁיטָא, חוּלִּין נִינְהוּ! אֶלָּא דְּאִיעַבַּר לִפְנֵי פִּדְיוֹנָן, וְאִתְיְלִיד לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנָן.

b1.he: נִפְדִּין תְּמִימִים אוֹ אֵין נִפְדִּין תְּמִימִין?

b2.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַמַּתְפִּיס בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין קְבוּעִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, וְיָלְדוּ — יִמָּכְרוּ, וְאֵין צְרִיכִין מוּם, שֶׁאֵין קְדוּשָּׁה חָלָה עֲלֵיהֶן, שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא טָפֵל חָמוּר מִן הָעִיקָּר.

b3.he: טַעְמָא, שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא טָפֵל חָמוּר מִן הָעִיקָּר, אֲבָל הִקְדִּישׁ זָכָר לְדָמָיו — קָדוֹשׁ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף. מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרָבָא, דְּאָמַר רָבָא: הִקְדִּישׁ זָכָר לְדָמָיו — קָדוֹשׁ קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף.

b4.he: וְהַשּׁוֹחֲטָן בַּחוּץ פָּטוּר. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מַתְנֵי ״חַיָּיב״, וּמוֹקֵי לַהּ בְּבָמַת יָחִיד.

b5.he: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִנַּיִן לַזּוֹבֵחַ בְּהֵמָה בַּעֲלַת מוּם בְּבָמַת יָחִיד בִּשְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר הַבָּמוֹת, שֶׁהוּא בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לֹא תִזְבַּח לַה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ שׁוֹר וָשֶׂה״, אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְבָמָה גְּדוֹלָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״עַוֶּרֶת אוֹ שָׁבוּר וְגוֹ׳״, תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְבָמַת יָחִיד.

b6.he: אֵימָא: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְקָדָשִׁים — תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לִבְכוֹר, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וְקָדוֹשׁ כְּשֶׁהוּא בַּעַל מוּם — לִיקְרַב נָמֵי כְּשֶׁהוּא בַּעַל מוּם, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּלָא!

b7.he: אָמְרִי: בְּכוֹר בְּהֶדְיָא כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ ״פִּסֵּחַ אוֹ עִוֵּר לֹא תִזְבָּחֶנּוּ״.

b8.he: וְאֵימָא: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְקָדָשִׁים — תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְמַעֲשֵׂר, דְּסָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וְקָדוֹשׁ בְּמוּמוֹ, דִּכְתִיב: ״לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין טוֹב לָרַע״, נִקְרַב נָמֵי בְּמוּמֵיהּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּלָא!

b10.he: אֵימָא: תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לִתְמוּרַת קָדָשִׁים, דְּסָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וּקְדוֹשָׁה כְּשֶׁהִיא בַּעֲלַת מוּם, דִּכְתִיב: ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר אוֹתוֹ וְגוֹ׳״, קָרֵיבָה נָמֵי כְּשֶׁהִיא בַּעֲלַת מוּם, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּלָא!

b11.he: אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְהָיָה הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ״, מַקִּישׁ תְּמוּרָתוֹ לוֹ — מָה הוּא בַּעַל מוּם לֹא, אַף תְּמוּרָתוֹ בַּעַל מוּם לֹא.

b12.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: אֵימָא, תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְוַלְדוֹת קָדָשִׁים, דְּסָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וּקְדוֹשִׁין כְּשֶׁהֵן בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין אַגַּב אִמָּן, כְּשֶׁהֵן בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין נָמֵי קָרְבִי, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּלָא!

b13.he: אָמַר רָבָא: כְּבָר פַּסְקַהּ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: ״רַק קָדָשֶׁיךָ אֲשֶׁר יִהְיוּ לְךָ וּנְדָרֶיךָ״ — ״רַק קָדָשֶׁיךָ״ אֵלּוּ הַתְּמוּרוֹת, ״אֲשֶׁר יִהְיוּ לְךָ״ אֵלּוּ הַוְּולָדוֹת, ״וּנְדָרֶיךָ״ — הִקִּישָׁן הַכָּתוּב לְנֶדֶר, מָה נֶדֶר בַּעַל מוּם לֹא, אַף הָנֵי נָמֵי בַּעַל מוּם לֹא.

b14.he: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה, מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר וְגוֹ׳״. הַשְׁתָּא רַע בְּטוֹב אָמְרַתְּ לֹא, טוֹב בְּרָע מִיבַּעְיָא? אֶלָּא טוֹב מֵעִיקָּרוֹ עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה, רַע מֵעִיקָּרוֹ אֵין עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה.

b15.he: אִם מֵתוּ יִפָּדוּ. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דְּאָמַר: קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת לֹא הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה.

b16.he: דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת, אִם מֵתוּ — יִפָּדוּ. וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּבַעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ שֶׁנִּפְדֶּה. מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״אוֹתָהּ״ ״אוֹתָהּ״ — לְמַעוֹטֵי בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרָא.

b17.he: אֲבָל חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אִם מֵתוּ — יִקָּבֵרוּ. מַאן חֲכָמִים? תָּנָא דְּבֵי לֵוִי הוּא, דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי לֵוִי: הַכֹּל הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, וַאֲפִילּוּ בַּעַל מוּם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ.

b18.he: וְכֵן תָּנָא דְּבֵי לֵוִי בְּמַתְנִיתֵיהּ: אֲפִילּוּ חַיָּה, אֲפִילּוּ עוֹף, וְהָכְתִיב ״אוֹתָהּ״! ״אוֹתָהּ״ לְתָנָא דְּבֵי לֵוִי קַשְׁיָא.

b19.he: אֲבָל רַבָּנַן דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, מַאי? הָכִי נָמֵי דְּאִם מֵתוּ יִפָּדוּ? אִי הָכִי,

messages.text: 13b closed the discussion of how a Jew acquires property from a gentile, by payment or by pulling. Here a new mishna begins: consecrated animals whose permanent blemish came before their consecration, and those whose consecration came first.
Mishna

All sacrificial animals in which a permanent blemish preceded their consecration do not assume inherent sanctity and only their value is consecrated, and once they were redeemed, they are obligated in the mitzva of a firstborn, i.e., their offspring are subject to being counted a firstborn, and in the priestly gifts of the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw,

notes.dh: מתני' כל הקדשים שקדם מום קבוע להקדשן
notes.he: שהיה להם מום קבוע והקדישן להמכר ולהבא מדמיהם קרבן למזבח:
notes.en: MISHNA. All sacrificial animals in which a permanent blemish preceded their consecration: they had a permanent blemish, and he consecrated them to be sold, so that an offering for the altar would be brought with their money.

notes.he: לאחר פדיונן אם ילדו:
notes.en: They are obligated in the firstborn: after their redemption, if they gave birth.

notes.he: זרוע לחיים וקיבה כחולין גמורין:
notes.en: And in the gifts: the foreleg, the jaw and the maw, like fully non-sacred animals.

notes.dh: כל הקדשים שקדם מום קבוע להקדשן
notes.he: לאו בקדשי בדק הבית איירי אלא בהקדישן למזבח לדמיהן דאין חילוק בין רישא לסיפא אלא שזה קדם הקדשו למומו וזה קדם מומו להקדשו ואע"פ שעובר כשהקדיש בעל מום למזבח כדאמרינן פ"ק דתמורה (דף ו:) מכל מקום אשמעינן דינו והתם מפרש מאי שנא מדקלא בעלמא ומשני בריא מילתא טפי שביק תמים ומקדשין בעלי מומין:
notes.en: All sacrificial animals in which a permanent blemish preceded their consecration: this does not speak of items consecrated for Temple maintenance, but of one who consecrated them for the altar, for their value. For there is no difference between the first clause and the latter clause except that in this one the blemish preceded the consecration and in that one the consecration preceded the blemish. And although one transgresses when he consecrates a blemished animal for the altar, as we say in the first chapter of Temura (6b), in any case the mishna teaches us its law. And there the Gemara asks how this differs from [consecrating] a mere palm tree, and answers: the matter is more pointed, since he passes over unblemished animals and consecrates blemished ones.

messages.text: and they can emerge from their sacred status and assume complete non-sacred status in order to be shorn and to be utilized for labor.

notes.he: בפדיונן לגמרי ליגזז וליעבד כחולין גרידי משום דמעיקרא לא חיילא עלייהו קדושה חמורה:
notes.en: And they emerge to non-sacred status: completely, through their redemption, to be shorn and worked like plain non-sacred animals, because the severe sanctity never took effect on them in the first place.

notes.he: אע"ג דשאר פסולי המוקדשין אסירי בגיזה ועבודה כיון דמום קדם להקדש מותרין:
notes.en: And they emerge to non-sacred status to be shorn and worked: even though other disqualified consecrated animals are forbidden in shearing and labor, since the blemish preceded the consecration, these are permitted.

messages.text: And their offspring and their milk are permitted after their redemption.

notes.he: להכי [מותר] הנאתו לאחר פדיונן דאע"ג דאיעבר לפני פדיונן כיון דיליד לאחר פדיונן מותר בלא פדייה:
notes.en: And their offspring and their milk are permitted after their redemption: this is why benefit from it is permitted after their redemption: even though it was conceived before their redemption, since it was born after their redemption, it is permitted without redemption.

messages.text: And one who slaughters them outside the Temple courtyard is exempt from karet,

notes.he: אפי' קודם פדיון דאפי' הוי מומן קל כגון דוקין שבעין דלגבי קדשים מיחייב השוחטן בחוץ הכא פטור משום דלא חלה עליהן מתחילה קדושה כל כך:
notes.en: And one who slaughters them outside is exempt: even before their redemption. Even if their blemish is a minor one, such as pale spots in the eye, for which one who slaughters ordinary sacrificial animals outside is liable, here he is exempt, because so great a sanctity never took effect on them in the first place.

notes.he: חוץ לעזרה:
notes.en: And one who slaughters them outside: outside the Temple courtyard.

messages.text: and those animals do not render an animal that was a substitute for them consecrated.

notes.he: מפרש בגמ':
notes.en: And they do not render a substitute: this is explained in the Gemara.

notes.he: אפי' קודם פדיונן:
notes.en: And they do not render a substitute: even before their redemption.

messages.text: And if these animals died before they were redeemed, they may be redeemed and fed to dogs, and they do not require burial, except for the firstborn and the animal tithe. With regard to these two types of offerings, even if they were blemished before they became consecrated they assume inherent sanctity, like other offerings that were consecrated and subsequently became blemished.

notes.he: קודם פדיונן יפדו להאכילן לכלבים דאין קדושתן חמורה ותו קמ"ל דגרעי משאר קדשים שאין נפדין אלא חיין שיוכלו לעמוד בפני הכהן בשעת הערכתן דכתיב (ויקרא כז) והעמיד (הכהן) את הבהמה וגו' והדר והעריך (אותה) הכהן וגו':
notes.en: And if they died: before their redemption, they are redeemed in order to feed them to the dogs, since their sanctity is not severe. And it further teaches us that they are lesser than other sacrificial animals, which are redeemed only alive, so that they can stand before the priest at the time of their valuation, as it is written: “Then he shall stand the animal [before the priest],” and afterward, “And the priest shall appraise it” (Leviticus 27:11–12).

notes.he: שאפילו במומן חלה עליהן קדושה חמורה דבכור רחם מקדשו ובמעשר כתיב (שם) לא יבקר בין טוב לרע דמשמע בין תם בין בעל מום קדוש טוב תם רע בעל מום:
notes.en: Except for the firstborn and the tithe: for even with their blemish the severe sanctity takes effect on them. The firstborn, because the womb sanctifies it; and of the tithe it is written: “He shall not inquire whether it be good or bad” (Leviticus 27:33), which implies that whether it is unblemished or blemished it is sacred: “good” is unblemished, “bad” is blemished.

notes.he: דאע"ג (דקבע דם) [נ"ל דקדם] מום קבוע להקדישן:
notes.en: Except for the firstborn and the tithe: for even though a permanent blemish preceded their consecration [they are fully sacred]. [The printed text is garbled here; the editor’s correction reads “preceded”.]

messages.text: And all sacrificial animals whose consecration preceded their blemish, or who had a temporary blemish prior to their consecration and afterward developed a permanent blemish and they were redeemed, they are exempt from, i.e., their offspring are not counted, a firstborn, and from the gifts of the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw, and they do not completely emerge from their sacred status and assume non-sacred status in order to be shorn and to be utilized for labor.

notes.he: כמאן דליתיה דמי וחלה עליהן קדושה:
notes.en: A temporary blemish: it is as though it were not there, and sanctity takes effect on them.

notes.he: מפרש בגמרא:
notes.en: Exempt from the firstborn: this is explained in the Gemara.

notes.he: שאפי' לאחר פדיונן אסורין (בהנאה) בגיזה ועבודה כדמפרש בגמרא:
notes.en: And they do not emerge, etc.: for even after their redemption they are forbidden in shearing and labor, as the Gemara explains.

notes.he: מ"מ דינן כקדשין ופטורין מן הבכורה והמתנות משום דקדושתן באה מאיליה והוו קדושת הגוף. ואי אמרת בכור היאך יוכל לקדם מום להקדישו והלא קדושתו מרחם כגון שהומם במעי אמו קודם שיקדשו יציאת הרחם:
notes.en: And they were redeemed: in any case their law is like that of sacrificial animals, and they are exempt from the firstborn and the gifts, because their sanctity came of itself and it is inherent sanctity. And if you say: with a firstborn, how can a blemish precede its consecration, when its sanctity is from the womb? For example, where it was blemished in its mother’s womb, before the exit from the womb sanctified it.

messages.text: And their offspring, which were conceived prior to redemption, and their milk, are prohibited after their redemption.

notes.he: מפרש בגמרא כשנתעברו קודם פדיונן וילדו לאחר פדיונן:
notes.en: Their offspring and their milk are prohibited, etc.: the Gemara explains: where they became pregnant before their redemption and gave birth after their redemption.

messages.text: And one who slaughters them outside the Temple courtyard is liable to receive karet, and those animals render an animal that was a substitute for them consecrated. And if these animals died before they were redeemed, they may not be redeemed and fed to dogs; rather, they must be buried.

notes.he: קודם פדיונן:
notes.en: And one who slaughters them outside: before their redemption.

notes.he: כרת. ובגמרא מפרש בדוקין שבעין דראוין הן לפנים ואליבא דרבי עקיבא דאמר אם עלו לא ירדו אבל בשאר מומין לא דאמרינן במסכת יומא (דף סג:) הראוי לאהל מועד חייבין עליו אי לא לא:
notes.en: Is liable: to karet. And in the Gemara it is explained as referring to pale spots in the eye, which are fit [to be brought] inside, and in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, who says that if they were brought up [onto the altar] they are not taken down. But with other blemishes, no, for we say in Tractate Yoma (63b): Whatever is fit for the Tent of Meeting, one is liable for it; if not, not.

notes.he: ואין נפדין דבעי העמדה והערכה:
notes.en: They must be buried: and they are not redeemed, because they require standing and valuation.

messages.caption: The mishna’s two cases side by side: a permanent blemish before consecration, or consecration before the blemish.

messages.text: Gemara

The mishna teaches that all animals that were blemished prior to their consecration are subject to their offspring being counted a firstborn and to the obligation of the gifts once they have been redeemed. The Gemara infers: The reason that they are subject to the obligations of a firstborn and the gifts is that they were redeemed. But if they were not redeemed, they are exempt from their offspring being counted a firstborn and from the obligation of the priestly gifts.
messages.quote: and once they were redeemed, they are obligated in the mitzva of a firstborn

notes.he: ארישא קאי:
notes.en: GEMARA. The reason is that they were redeemed: this refers to the first clause.

messages.text: This indicates that the tanna of the mishna holds: Sanctity that inheres in an animal’s value defers, i.e., renders it exempt, from the mitzva of the firstborn and from the gifts.

notes.he: פטורה מן הבכורה כקדושת הגוף דמפרש לקמן מקראי דפטורה מבכורה וממתנות:
notes.en: Sanctity of value: exempts from the firstborn just like inherent sanctity, as is explained below from verses that it exempts from the firstborn and from the gifts.

notes.dh: קדושת דמים מדחה מן הבכורה ומן המתנות
notes.he: פי' הקונטרס קדושת דמים פוטרת מן הבכורה כקדושת הגוף כדמפרש לקמן מקראי דפוטרת מן הבכורה ומן המתנות וקשה לפי' דהתם פטרינן בפסולי המוקדשין אע"פ דנפדו מדאיתקש לצבי ואיל והכא דוקא בלא נפדו אלא היינו טעמא בקדושת דמים משום דכתיב (במדבר ג׳:י״ג) גבי בכור בישראל ובמתנות כתיב (דברים יח) מאת העם:
notes.en: Sanctity of value defers from the firstborn and from the gifts: the Kuntres [Rashi] explained: sanctity of value exempts from the firstborn like inherent sanctity, as is explained below from verses that it exempts from the firstborn and from the gifts. This is difficult for his explanation, for there we exempt disqualified consecrated animals even though they were redeemed, since they are compared to the gazelle and the deer, whereas here [the exemption is] specifically when they were not redeemed. Rather, this is the reason with sanctity of value: because regarding the firstborn it is written “in Israel” (Numbers 3:13), and regarding the gifts it is written “from the people” (Deuteronomy 18:3).

notes.dh: קדושת דמים מדחה מן הבכורה ומן המתנות
notes.he: דכיון דקדם מום קבוע להקדשן ההוא הקדש לא הוי אלא קדושת דמים שימכרו ויביא בדמיהן קדשים. ואפי' הכי אי לא מפדו פטורין מן הבכורה ומן המתנות:
notes.en: Sanctity of value defers from the firstborn and from the gifts: since a permanent blemish preceded their consecration, that consecration is only sanctity of value, that they be sold and sacrificial animals brought with their money. And even so, if they are not redeemed they are exempt from the firstborn and from the gifts.

messages.text: The Gemara infers: The reason they become non-sacred is that they were redeemed. But if they were not redeemed, they remain sacred and are prohibited with regard to shearing and labor.
messages.quote: And they can emerge from their sacred status and assume complete non-sacred status

notes.he: קודם פדיונן:
notes.en: Forbidden in shearing and labor: before their redemption.

messages.text: This supports the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, who says:

notes.he: והני כקדשי בדק הבית דמו דהם עצמן לא הוקדשו מתחילה אלא לדמיהן:
notes.en: Items consecrated for Temple maintenance, etc.: and these are like items consecrated for Temple maintenance, since they themselves were consecrated from the outset only for their value.

messages.text: Animals consecrated for the Temple maintenance are prohibited with regard to shearing and labor.

notes.he: קדושת דמים נינהו שימכרו לצורך תיקון בדק הבית:
notes.en: Items consecrated for Temple maintenance: they are sanctity of value, to be sold for the needs of the Temple’s repair.

messages.text: Since animals consecrated for the Temple maintenance are equivalent to animals that possess sanctity that inheres in their value, the mishna supports Rabbi Eliezer’s opinion.

The Sages said: No; the mishna does not necessarily support the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer. It is possible that it is only with regard to an animal that has sanctity that inheres in its value and that was consecrated for the altar, which can be mistakenly exchanged with an animal that possesses inherent sanctity and was likewise consecrated for the altar, that the Sages decreed that it is prohibited to shear it and perform labor with it, due to a concern that one might confuse it with an animal that possesses inherent sanctity and ultimately violate a Torah prohibition.
messages.quote: consecrated for the Temple maintenance are prohibited with regard to shearing and labor

notes.he: תסייעיה ממתניתין דקדושת דמים למזבח הוא דהוקדשו לשם כן שיהיו הדמים קריבין למזבח והתם הוא דאסור בגיזה ועבודה משום דמיחלפא בקדושת הגוף למזבח:
notes.en: No: do not bring support from our mishna. Here it is sanctity of value for the altar, for they were consecrated for that purpose, that their money be offered on the altar, and there it is forbidden in shearing and labor because it can be confused with inherent sanctity for the altar.

notes.he: מיהא לא מסייעא ליה לר' אליעזר דהיינו טעמא דתנא דמתני' דאסר להו בגיזה ועבודה כי לא ניפדו משום דהני שהוקדשו במומן קדושת דמים למזבח הוא שימכרו ויביאו מדמיהן קדשים תמימין למזבח ואי שרית להו בגיזה ועבודה אתי לאחלופי למישרי בקדושת המזבח. קדשי בדק הבית דלא הוו קדושת דמים למזבח דליכא לאיחלופי בהו לא גזרו בהו רבנן דליהוו אסירי בגיזה ועבודה ומיהא לא מסייעא ליה:
notes.en: They said: No. In any case it does not support Rabbi Eliezer. For this is the reason of the tanna of our mishna, who forbids them in shearing and labor when they were not redeemed: these, which were consecrated with their blemish, are sanctity of value for the altar, that they be sold and unblemished offerings brought for the altar with their money; and if you permit them in shearing and labor, people will come to confuse them and permit [the same] with sanctity of the altar. Items consecrated for Temple maintenance, which are not sanctity of value for the altar and cannot be confused, the Rabbis did not decree to be forbidden in shearing and labor. So in any case it does not support him.

messages.text: But with regard to animals consecrated for the Temple maintenance, no such decree was issued, as this concern does not apply.

What are the circumstances of the case of the mishna, in which the offspring of blemished redeemed animals are permitted? If we say that the mishna is referring to a case where the animals became pregnant and gave birth after their redemption, then it is obvious that the offspring are permitted, as they are non-sacred animals from the moment of conception.
messages.quote: their offspring and their milk are permitted after their redemption

messages.text: Rather, it must be referring to a case where they became pregnant before their redemption, and gave birth after their redemption, and the mishna is teaching that the offspring are permitted despite the fact they were conceived while their mothers were consecrated.
The Gemara infers from this ruling: But if the animals gave birth before their redemption, the offspring are prohibited until they are redeemed.

notes.he: ולדות שנולדו לפני פדיונן אסורין בהנאה בלא פדייה ומיקרב לא קרבי דמכח קדושה דחויה אתו דאמם לא הוקדשה למזבח:
notes.en: But [before their redemption]: offspring born before their redemption are forbidden in benefit without redemption. And they are not offered, since they come from the force of a deferred sanctity, for their mother was not consecrated for the altar [itself].

notes.he: דאיעבר ואתיליד קודם פדיונן אסירי אותן וולדות בלא פדיון:
notes.en: But before: where they were conceived and born before their redemption, those offspring are forbidden without redemption.

messages.text: The halakha is that the offspring of an animal that possesses inherent sanctity is born sanctified, and therefore it cannot be redeemed until it develops a blemish.

With regard to the offspring of an animal that possesses sanctity that inheres in its value, are they redeemed unblemished, or are they not redeemed unblemished? In other words, can they be redeemed immediately, or must one wait until they develop a blemish?

notes.he: אותן וולדות שנולדו לפני פדיונן או אין נפדין תמימים:
notes.en: Are they redeemed unblemished: those offspring that were born before their redemption; or are they not redeemed unblemished?

notes.he: אותן וולדות:
notes.en: Are they redeemed unblemished: those offspring.

notes.he: דצריך להמתין להן עד שיוממו ואח"כ פודן:
notes.en: Or are they not redeemed unblemished: so that one must wait with them until they become blemished, and afterward redeem them.

messages.text: Come and hear a proof from a baraita:

With regard to one who dedicates permanently blemished animals for the altar, and those animals gave birth, their offspring may be sold in order to be redeemed and they do not require a blemish to render their sale permitted. The reason is that they are not imbued with sanctity, and that the subsidiary sanctity of the offspring should not be more stringent than the primary sanctity of the mother.

notes.he: ולד:
notes.en: Subsidiary: the offspring.

notes.he: אם. אלמא נפדין תמימים:
notes.en: Primary: the mother. Evidently they are redeemed unblemished.

notes.he: (לא) המתפיס בעלי מומין קבועין לגבי מזבח היינו דקדם מומן להקדישן וילדו קודם פדיונן. ימכרו ואין צריכין מום אותן וולדות להמתין שלא למוכרן עד שיפול בהן מום:
notes.en: Rav Amram taught: [Rabbeinu Gershom’s text reads “Rav Amram taught” where ours reads “Come and hear.”] One who dedicates permanently blemished animals for the altar: that is, where their blemish preceded their consecration, and they gave birth before their redemption. They may be sold and they do not require a blemish: there is no need to wait with those offspring and not sell them until a blemish befalls them.

notes.he: (שלא) משום דקא אתו הני מכח קדושה דחויה:
notes.en: [That they are not imbued with sanctity:] because these come from the force of a deferred sanctity.

notes.he: הוולדות שאינן קדושין אלא אגב אימן:
notes.en: That the subsidiary should not: the offspring, which are sanctified only by virtue of their mother.

messages.text: Since the blemished mother can be redeemed without delay, the same applies to its offspring. This proves that the offspring of animals that possess sanctity that inheres in their value may be redeemed.

notes.he: מן אימן אלא כשם שאימן יכול לפדות בכל עת כך וולדן נפדין אימתי שירצה אפילו תמימין אלמא דנפדין תמימין. והשתא דייק לברייתא טעמא דמשום הכי נפדין תמימין שלא יהא טפל חמור. הא הקדיש זכר תם לדמיו דאע"ג דאמר איני מקדישו אלא לדמיו קדיש קדושת הגוף הואיל (ואביו) [והוה] ראוי להקרבה ואין נפדה תמים. והאי דקאמר הא הקדיש זכר תם הוא הדין לנקבה אלא משום דבעי לסיועי מינה לרבא ורבא לא איירי אלא בזכר כדאמר בתמורה בפרק אלו קדשים אמר רבא זאת אומרת הקדיש זכר כו' נקט הכא זכר כו':
notes.en: Be more stringent than the primary: than their mother. Rather, just as their mother can be redeemed at any time, so too their offspring are redeemed whenever he wishes, even unblemished. Evidently they are redeemed unblemished. And now he infers from the baraita: the reason they are redeemed unblemished is that the subsidiary should not be more stringent; but if he consecrated an unblemished male for its value, even though he said, “I consecrate it only for its value,” it is sanctified with inherent sanctity, since it is fit to be offered, and it is not redeemed unblemished. And though it says “but if he consecrated an unblemished male,” the same is true of a female; it says “male” here only because it wants to support Rava, and Rava speaks only of a male, as is said in Temura, chapter Elu Kodashim: Rava said: That is to say, one who consecrates a male, etc.

messages.text: The reason that the baraita rules that the sanctity for the altar does not take effect is that the subsidiary sanctity should not be more stringent than the primary sanctity, i.e., the only reason it is not sanctified for the altar is because its sanctity is derived from its mother, which cannot be sanctified for the altar as it is blemished.

notes.he: וקא דייק הש"ס טעמא דלא בעי מום משום דלא יהא טפל חמור מן העיקר דמכח בעל מום אתו הא לא אתו מכח בעל מום אלא לדידהו מקדיש להו לדמיהן לא נפקי לחולין בלא מום דקדוש קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: And the Gemara infers: the reason it does not require a blemish is that the subsidiary should not be more stringent than the primary, since they come from the force of a blemished animal. But animals that do not come from the force of a blemished animal, but one consecrates them themselves for their value, do not go out to non-sacred status without a blemish, for they are sanctified with inherent sanctity.

messages.text: But if one consecrated an unblemished male animal for its value, where there is no secondary consecration, it is sanctified with inherent sanctity. This supports the opinion of Rava, as Rava says:

notes.he: איל:
notes.en: Male: a ram.

notes.dh: הקדיש זכר לדמיו קדוש קדושת הגוף
notes.he: להכי נקט זכר דקרב הוא עצמו עולה ואי הוה נקט בהמה סתם הוי אמינא דנקבה קדוש קדושת הגוף וקרב שלמים ושמעינן ליה לר' יהושע במסכת שקלים (דף ו.) ומייתי לה בתמורה פרק אלו קדשים (תמורה דף כ.) במקדיש נכסיו זכרים עצמן יקרבו עולות ונקבות ימכרו לצרכי שלמים ויביא בדמיהם עולות ומיהו נראה לר' אליעזר נמי דאמר התם זכרים ימכרו לצרכי עולות ונקבות ימכרו לצרכי שלמים ודמיהם יפלו לשאר נכסים לבדק הבית לפי מה שהיה רבא ר"ל מתחלה התם בההוא פירקין המקדיש זכר אין קדוש קדושת הגוף לא קשה ליה מידי ממתני' דשקלים דיש לחלק בין מקדיש נכסיו סתם לפירש בהדיא לדמיו:
notes.en: He consecrated a male for its value; it is sanctified with inherent sanctity: that is why it says “male,” because it itself is offered as a burnt offering. Had it said simply “an animal,” I would have said that a female too is sanctified with inherent sanctity and is offered as a peace offering. And we hear from Rabbi Yehoshua in Tractate Shekalim (6a), cited in Temura, chapter Elu Kodashim (Temura 20a), regarding one who consecrates his property: the males themselves are offered as burnt offerings, and the females are sold for the needs of peace offerings and burnt offerings are brought with their money. However, it seems that for Rabbi Eliezer too, who says there that the males are sold for the needs of burnt offerings and the females are sold for the needs of peace offerings, and their money goes with the rest of the property to Temple maintenance, and according to what Rava wanted to say at first there in that chapter, that one who consecrates a male is not sanctified with inherent sanctity, there is no difficulty at all from the mishna in Shekalim: one can distinguish between one who consecrates his property without specifying and one who stated explicitly “for its value.”

messages.text: If one consecrated a male animal for its value, it is sanctified with inherent sanctity.

notes.he: שימכרנו ויביא בדמיו עולה הוא עצמו קדוש קדושת הגוף ויקרב עולה. להכי נקט זכר דחזי לעולה משום דרובא דמייתו קרבן עולה מייתו:
notes.en: He consecrated a male for its value: that he would sell it and bring a burnt offering with its money; it itself is sanctified with inherent sanctity and is offered as a burnt offering. That is why it says “male”: because it is fit for a burnt offering, for most people who bring an offering bring a burnt offering.

messages.text: Rabbi Elazar teaches the mishna as follows: And one who slaughters them outside the Temple courtyard is liable, and he interprets the mishna as referring to a case of a private altar of an individual.
messages.lead: § The mishna teaches with regard to animals whose blemish preceded their consecration:
messages.quote: And one who slaughters them outside the Temple courtyard is exempt

notes.he: השוחט בחוץ חייב. לאו כרת קאמר אלא מלקות:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar teaches: one who slaughters outside is liable. He does not mean karet but lashes.

notes.he: להאי חוץ כגון ששחטו בבמת יחיד בשעת היתר הבמות:
notes.en: And he interprets: this “outside” as, for example, where he slaughtered it on a private altar at the time when private altars were permitted.

messages.text: In other words, the mishna is not teaching that one is liable to receive karet for slaughtering an animal outside the Temple courtyard, but that he is liable to receive lashes for sacrificing a blemished animal upon a private altar.

notes.he: ומוקים לה בבמת יחיד וכ"ש דחייב בבמת צבור ומשום הכי קרי ליה חוץ שאין שם עזרה וחייב משום דמקריב בעל מום בבמה בשעת היתר הבמות. והיכן הותרו כדאמרי' באו לנוב ולגבעון הותרו הבמות כו':
notes.en: And he interprets it as a private altar: and all the more so he is liable at a public altar. And that is why it calls it “outside,” since there is no courtyard there. And he is liable because he offers a blemished animal at an altar at the time when private altars were permitted. And when were they permitted? As we say: When they came to Nov and Givon, private altars were permitted, etc.

messages.text: From where is it derived that one who slaughters a blemished animal upon a private altar of an individual at a time when private altars are permitted is in violation of a prohibition? It is derived from a verse, as it is stated: “You shall not sacrifice to the Lord an ox, or a sheep, in which is a blemish”.

verse.he: לֹא־תִזְבַּח לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ שׁוֹר וָשֶׂה אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בוֹ מוּם כֹּל דָּבָר רָע כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ הוּא׃ {ס}
verse.en: You shall not sacrifice to the ETERNAL your God an ox or a sheep that has any defect of a serious kind, for that is abhorrent to the ETERNAL your God.

notes.he: שכל אחד ואחד בונה במה לעצמו כגון במת מנוח וגדעון ושמואל:
notes.en: A private altar: that each and every one builds an altar for himself, such as the altars of Manoaḥ, Gideon and Samuel.

messages.text: If this verse is not referring to the matter of a great public altar, since that halakha is derived from a different verse, as it is written: “Blind or broken…you shall not sacrifice these unto the Lord”, apply the verse in Deuteronomy to the matter of a private altar of an individual.

verse.he: עַוֶּרֶת אוֹ שָׁבוּר אוֹ־חָרוּץ אוֹ־יַבֶּלֶת אוֹ גָרָב אוֹ יַלֶּפֶת לֹא־תַקְרִיבוּ אֵלֶּה לַיהֹוָה וְאִשֶּׁה לֹא־תִתְּנוּ מֵהֶם עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: Anything blind, or injured, or maimed, or with a wen, boil-scar, or scurvy—such you shall not offer to GOD; you shall not put any of them on the altar as offerings by fire to GOD.

notes.he: נוב וגבעון שהן של צבור:
notes.en: A great altar: Nov and Givon, which belonged to the public.

messages.text: But one can say with regard to the verse in Deuteronomy: If this verse is not referring to the matter of regular sacrificial animals, which is derived from the verse in Leviticus, apply it to the matter of a firstborn, as it might enter your mind to say: Since a firstborn animal is sanctified even when it is a permanently blemished animal, let it also be sacrificed upon the altar when it is a blemished animal.
messages.quote: You shall not sacrifice to the Lord an ox, or a sheep

notes.he: להיות אסור בגיזה ועבודה:
notes.en: Since it is sanctified when it is blemished: to be forbidden in shearing and labor.

notes.he: דריש הכי האי לא תזבח דאם אינו ענין לקדשים דהא כתיב עורת או שבור וכו':
notes.en: Say: expound this “You shall not sacrifice” thus: if it is not relevant to sacrificial animals, for it is already written: “Blind or broken,” etc.

messages.text: The verse in Deuteronomy would therefore teach us that this is not the halakha, i.e., a blemished firstborn animal may not be sacrificed upon the altar. What, then, is the reason that the halakha of a private altar of an individual, rather than the halakha of firstborn animals, is derived from the verse in Deuteronomy?

notes.dh: תנהו ענין לבכור דסד"א הואיל וקדיש במומיה
notes.he: ממילא כשנולד בעל מום [ה"א] שקרב נמי במומיה קמ"ל דלא תזבח דלא ולא אתא לבמת יחיד:
notes.en: Apply it to the matter of a firstborn, for it might enter your mind: since it is sanctified with its blemish of itself when it is born blemished, [I would say] it is also offered with its blemish. “You shall not sacrifice” teaches us that it is not, and then it would not come for a private altar.

messages.text: The Sages said in explanation: Concerning a firstborn, the halakha is written explicitly with regard to it: “Every firstborn…if there be any blemish therein, lameness, or blindness…you shall not sacrifice it”. Consequently, the verse in Deuteronomy, chapter 17, cannot be referring to the halakha that a firstborn animal may not be sacrificed upon the altar, as that is already taught in chapter 15.

verse.he: וְכִי־יִהְיֶה בוֹ מוּם פִּסֵּחַ אוֹ עִוֵּר כֹּל מוּם רָע לֹא תִזְבָּחֶנּוּ לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃
verse.en: But if it has a defect, lameness or blindness, any serious defect, you shall not sacrifice it to the ETERNAL your God.

notes.he: אמרי וכו' ואייתר לא תזבח לבמת יחיד:
notes.en: They said, etc.: and “You shall not sacrifice” remains free for a private altar.

messages.text: But still, one can say: If the verse in chapter 17 is not referring to the matter of sacrificial animals, which is derived from the verse in Leviticus, apply it to the matter of the animal tithe, as it might enter your mind to say: Since a tithed animal is sacred even with its blemish, as it is written: “He shall not inquire whether it be good or bad”, let it also be sacrificed with its blemish.

verse.he: לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין־טוֹב לָרַע וְלֹא יְמִירֶנּוּ וְאִם־הָמֵר יְמִירֶנּוּ וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לֹא יִגָּאֵל׃
verse.en: One must not look out for good as against bad, or make substitution for it. If one does make substitution for it, then it and its substitute shall both be holy: it cannot be redeemed.

notes.he: ולעולם בבמה גדולה:
notes.en: And say: if it is not relevant, etc.: and in fact [the verse speaks of] the great altar.

notes.he: לא יבדוק בין תם לבעל מום דאיזה שיהא עשירי יהא קדוש:
notes.en: He shall not inquire: he shall not examine between unblemished and blemished, for whichever is tenth shall be sacred.

notes.he: מאליו בשעבר תחת השבט דכתיב לא יבקר בין טוב לרע רע היינו בעל מום כדאמר לקמן:
notes.en: Since it is sanctified with its blemish: of itself, when it passes under the rod, as it is written: “He shall not inquire whether it be good or bad”; “bad” means a blemished animal, as is said below.

messages.text: The verse in Deuteronomy (17:1) would therefore teach us that this is not the halakha, i.e., a blemished tithed animal may not be sacrificed upon the altar.

The Sages said in response: With regard to the animal tithe as well, it is unnecessary for the verse to teach this halakha, as it is derived from a verbal analogy between the word: Passing, mentioned with regard to tithed animals (see Leviticus 27:32), and passing mentioned with regard to the firstborn (see Exodus 13:12). Just as a blemished firstborn animal is not sacrificed upon the altar, so too, a blemished tithed animal is not sacrificed upon the altar.

notes.he: מה בכור בעל מום לא קרב אף מעשר בעל מום לא כי אתא קרא לבמת יחיד:
notes.en: He derives “passing”, “passing” from the firstborn: just as a blemished firstborn is not offered, so too a blemished tithe is not. When the verse comes, it comes for a private altar.

notes.he: מצי למימר תחת תחת מקדשים ולפי שהמעשר ובכור שוין בכמה עניינים נקטיה:
notes.en: He derives “passing”: he could have said [a verbal analogy of] “in place of”, “in place of” from sacrificial animals; but because the tithe and the firstborn are alike in several matters, he chose it.

messages.text: But say that one should apply Deuteronomy 17:1 to the matter of animals substituted for sacrificial animals, as it might enter your mind to say: Since a substitute becomes sacred even when it is blemished, as it is written: “He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it, a good for a bad, or a bad for a good; and if he shall at all substitute animal for animal, then both it and that for which it is substituted shall be holy”, it may likewise be sacrificed when it is blemished.

verse.he: לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא־יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ־רַע בְּטוֹב וְאִם־הָמֵר יָמִיר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: One may not exchange or substitute another for it, either good for bad, or bad for good; if one does substitute one animal for another, the thing vowed and its substitute shall both be holy.

notes.he: דהיינו בעל מום אם המר ימיר יהיה קדש אפילו בעל מום:
notes.en: He shall not exchange it, a good for a bad: that is, a blemished one; “if he shall at all substitute, it shall be holy,” even a blemished one.

notes.he: הואיל וקדשה כשהיא בעל מום דכתי' לא ימיר אותו טוב ברע אם המר וגו':
notes.en: Since it is sanctified when it is blemished, as it is written: “He shall not exchange it…a good for a bad; and if he shall at all substitute,” etc.

messages.text: The verse in Deuteronomy would therefore teach us that this is not the halakha, as a blemished substitute cannot be sacrificed upon the altar.

The halakha with regard to a substitute is already established, as the verse states: “It and that for which it is substituted shall be holy.” The verse compares a substitute to the consecrated animal for which it was substituted: Just as the consecrated animal is not sacrificed if it is blemished, so too, its substitute is not sacrificed if it is blemished.

Say instead that one should apply it to the matter of the offspring of sacrificial animals, as it could enter your mind to say: Since they are sacred even when they are blemished, on account of their mother, they may also be sacrificed when they are blemished. Deuteronomy 17:1 would therefore teach us that this is not the halakha.
messages.lead: Rabbi Zeira objects to the claim that Deuteronomy 17:1 should be understood as referring to a private altar of an individual:

notes.he: בעלי מומין שנולדו מקדשים תמימים:
notes.en: Offspring: blemished ones born of unblemished sacrificial animals.

notes.dh: הואיל וקדשו [אגב] אימן כשהן בעלי מומין
notes.he: כשנולדו בעלי מומין או כשאירע להן אחר מיכן:
notes.en: Since they are sanctified [by virtue of] their mother when they are blemished: whether they were born blemished or it happened to them afterward.

messages.text: The tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael has already ruled that the blemished offspring of sacrificial animals cannot be sacrificed upon the altar, from a different verse. As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:

notes.he: מקרא אחרינא ולא איצטריך האי להכי:
notes.en: The tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael has already ruled: from another verse, and this one is not needed for that.

messages.text: The verse states: “Only your sacred items which you have, and your vows, you shall take, and go to the place which the Lord shall choose”. “Only your sacred items”; these are the substitutes. “Which you have”; these are the offspring.

verse.he: רַק קׇדָשֶׁיךָ אֲשֶׁר־יִהְיוּ לְךָ וּנְדָרֶיךָ תִּשָּׂא וּבָאתָ אֶל־הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en: But such sacred and votive donations as you may have shall be taken by you to the site that GOD will choose.

notes.he: דאתא לאשמועינן שיקרבו למזבח דאי לעיקר הקדש אתא למה לי למכתב שיעלם לירושלים הא שמעינן קראי טובא השמר לך פן תעלה עולותיך וגו':
notes.en: Only your sacred items, etc.: these are the substitutes: it comes to teach us that they are offered on the altar. For if it came for the principal consecration, why do I need it written that one should bring them up to Jerusalem? We already know that from many verses: “Take heed to yourself lest you offer your burnt offerings,” etc. (Deuteronomy 12:13).

notes.he: של קדשים:
notes.en: The offspring: of sacrificial animals.

messages.text: When it states: “And your vows,” the verse thereby juxtaposes animal substitutes and offspring with an animal consecrated by a vow, teaching that just as an animal consecrated by a vow is not sacrificed if it is blemished, so too, these are also not sacrificed if they are blemished.

notes.he: הלכך כי אתא לא תזבח לבמת יחיד אתא:
notes.en: So too these, when blemished, are not: therefore, when “You shall not sacrifice” comes, it comes for a private altar.

notes.he: אינו מן (כן) הברייתא בתמורה פרק אלו קדשים (תמורה דף יז:) ורבא מפרש כן בפני עצמו ולקמן (בכורות דף טו:) בשמעתין יש ברייתא אחרת דמפקא תמורת וולדות מזכר ונקבה ופליגא אתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל דהכא כדמפרש בתמורה (דף יז:) וכן פי' לקמן בקונטרס וההוא תנא נמי נפקא שפיר . שהקישה תמורות וולדות לגוף הקרבן דבגוף הקרבן איירי אם זכר ואם נקבה אלא דמיתורא דרשינן נמי תמורות וולדות ומהשתא לא צריכא להקישא דלעיל דמקיש תמורתו לו:
notes.en: He juxtaposed them to vows: this is not part of the baraita in Temura, chapter Elu Kodashim (Temura 17b); Rava explains it so on his own. And below (Bekhorot 15b), in our discussion, there is another baraita that derives substitutes and offspring from “male or female,” and it disagrees with the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael here, as explained in Temura (17b), and so Rashi explained below. That tanna too derives it well: the verse juxtaposed substitutes and offspring to the body of the offering, since “whether male or female” speaks of the body of the offering, except that from the extra wording we also expound substitutes and offspring. And on this view the juxtaposition above, which compares its substitute to it, is no longer needed.

messages.text: Accordingly, Deuteronomy 17:1 must be understood as referring to a private altar of an individual, as maintained by Rabbi Elazar.

notes.he: אמר רבא הא כבר פסקה כו' ואייתר ליה לא תזבח לבמת יחיד כדרבי אלעזר:
notes.en: Rava said: The tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael has already ruled, etc. And “You shall not sacrifice” remains free for a private altar, as Rabbi Elazar says.

messages.text: Tosafot note that “the verse juxtaposes them with a vow” is not in this baraita as it appears in Temura 17b, and read it as Rava’s own explanation. Here it follows the daf, as part of the baraita.
What is the reason for this ruling? It is derived from a verse, as the verse states: “He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it, a good for a bad, or a bad for a good”.
messages.quote: and those animals do not render an animal that was a substitute for them consecrated

verse.he: לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא־יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ־רַע בְּטוֹב וְאִם־הָמֵר יָמִיר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: One may not exchange or substitute another for it, either good for bad, or bad for good; if one does substitute one animal for another, the thing vowed and its substitute shall both be holy.

notes.he: השתא רע בטוב להחליף בעל מום בתמים:
notes.en: Now, bad for good: to exchange a blemished animal for an unblemished one.

messages.text: Now that you have said that substituting a bad animal for a good animal is not permitted, is it necessary to state that substituting a good animal for a bad animal is not permitted?

notes.he: שלא יביא בהמת חולין תמימים אצל בהמת קודש בעל מום ויאמר זו תמורת זו:
notes.en: Now that you have said bad for good is not: that he should not bring unblemished non-sacred animals beside a blemished sacred animal and say: This is the substitute of that.

notes.he: הך סוגיא דפ"ק דתמורה (דף ט.) ורבא סבר אין מזהירין (עונשין) מן הדין ודריש התם בע"א ואביי לא חשיב ליה דינא דמי גרעי ונקט הכא דרשא דאביי לפי שפשוט לו יותר וכהאי גוונא איכא בסנהדרין (דף לד:) גבי אין רואין את הנגעים אלא ביום ומייתי עלה דרשה דאביי דביום ולא בלילה ושביק דרשא דרבא דמפיק ליה מלי ולא לאורי ואין לתמוה מהא דאלו נשרפין (סנהדרין עו.) איכא איפכא גבי בתו מאנוסתו דאמר ק"ו בת בתו ענש על בתו לא כל שכן וחשיב ליה (לו) אביי גלוי מילתא טפי מרבא (ולא) גמרינן מהדדי דגבי אחותו איצטריך קרא לכולי עלמא לבת אביו ובת אמו משום דאין מזהירין מן הדין ולא חשיבא ליה גלויי מילתא בעלמא היינו משום דפשטיה דקרא משמע שבא למעט דכתיב בת אביו או בת אמו:
notes.en: In brief: Is it necessary to state good for bad? This discussion is from the first chapter of Temura (9a). There Rava holds that one does not derive a prohibition from an a fortiori inference and expounds the verse another way, while Abaye does not count this as an inference at all; here the Gemara takes Abaye’s derivation because it is plainer. Similarly in Sanhedrin (34b), on “one examines leprous marks only by day,” the Gemara brings Abaye’s derivation (“by day, and not by night”) and leaves aside Rava’s (from “to me, and not to my light”). One should not wonder at Elu Nisrafin (Sanhedrin 76a), where it seems the reverse with regard to one’s daughter from a woman he raped, derived a fortiori from his daughter’s daughter, which Abaye treats as merely revealing the meaning. There the two cases are not learned from each other: with regard to one’s sister a verse was needed by all opinions for a father’s daughter and a mother’s daughter, since one does not derive a prohibition a fortiori, and it is not treated as merely revealing the meaning because the plain sense of the verse, “his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter,” implies that it comes to exclude. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: ואם תאמר דלמא איצטריך משום סיפא דקרא והיה הוא ותמורתו יהיה קודש וי"ל דהוה מצי למיכתב בסיפיה ואם המר ימיר טוב ברע או רע בטוב:
notes.en: Is it necessary to state good for bad? And if you say: perhaps it was needed because of the end of the verse, “then both it and that for which it is substituted shall be holy”? One may say that it could have written that in its latter part: “And if he shall at all substitute good for bad or bad for good.”

notes.he: לכתחלה אבל דיעבד והיה הוא ותמורתו וגו':
notes.en: You have said no: at the outset; but after the fact, “then both it and that for which it is substituted shall be holy.”

notes.he: תמים בבעל מום מיבעיא דלכתחלה לא:
notes.en: Good for bad: is it necessary to state that unblemished for blemished is not permitted at the outset?

messages.text: Rather, the verse is teaching that an animal which is good at the outset renders an animal that was a substitute for it sacred, but an animal that is bad at the outset, i.e., whose blemish preceded its consecration, does not render an animal that was a substitute for it sacred.

notes.he: להכי כתיב טוב ברע:
notes.en: Rather: that is why “good for bad” is written.

notes.he: שנתפס בקדושה כשהוא תמים עושה תמורה אע"פ שהומם כדכתיב או רע בטוב דמשמע רע של קודש בטוב של חולין דרע של קודש עושה תמורה:
notes.en: Good at the outset: one that was caught in sanctity when it was unblemished makes a substitute even though it became blemished, as it is written: “or a bad for a good,” which implies a bad sacred animal for a good non-sacred one: a bad sacred animal makes a substitute.

notes.he: האי טוב ברע לא אתי אלא לאשמועינן דאותו טוב ברע דדיעבד עושה תמורה בעינן שיהא טוב מעיקרו שקדם הקדשו למומו. אבל רע מעיקרו שקדם מומו להקדשו לעולם אין עושה תמורה:
notes.en: Rather: this “good for bad” comes only to teach us that for a good-for-bad exchange to make a substitute after the fact, we require [the consecrated animal] to be good at the outset, its consecration having preceded its blemish. But one that is bad at the outset, whose blemish preceded its consecration, never makes a substitute.

messages.text: This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon, who says: Items consecrated to be sacrificed on the altar were included in the requirement of standing and valuation, but items with the sanctity of those consecrated for Temple maintenance, such as the red heifer, were not included in the requirement of standing and valuation.
messages.quote: And if these animals died before they were redeemed, they may be redeemed

notes.he: דאמר בפרק בתרא דתמורה (דף לב.) קדשי מזבח היו בכלל העמדה והערכה:
notes.en: This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon: who says in the last chapter of Temura (32a): Items consecrated for the altar were included in standing and valuation.

notes.he: קודם פדיונן יפדו ומותרין בהנאה עורן ונבלתן:
notes.en: And if they died: before their redemption, they are redeemed, and benefit from their hide and carcass is permitted.

notes.he: [זו דברי ר"ש] תנא דמתניתין דאמר אם מתו יפדו זו דברי ר"ש דאמר במס' תמורה בפרק אחרון קדשי מזבח היו בכלל העמדה וכו' אבל לא קדשי בדק הבית דקדושת דמים נינהו לא בעו העמדה:
notes.en: [This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon:] the tanna of our mishna, who says “if they died they are redeemed”: this is the statement of Rabbi Shimon, who says in Tractate Temura, in the last chapter: Items consecrated for the altar were included in standing [and valuation], etc., but not items consecrated for Temple maintenance, which are sanctity of value and do not require standing.

messages.text: Since animals that were consecrated for the altar require standing and valuation in order to be redeemed, they cannot be redeemed after death, as it is no longer possible to stand them before the priest. Animals consecrated for the Temple maintenance, and likewise animals whose blemish preceded their consecration, do not require standing and valuation, and therefore they can be redeemed after death.

With regard to animals consecrated for the Temple maintenance, if they died they may be redeemed, because animals consecrated for the Temple maintenance are not included in the obligation of standing and valuation.
messages.lead: This is as we learned in a mishna:

notes.he: ומדאמר רבי שמעון קדשי בדק הבית לא היו מכלל דקרא בקדשי מזבח כתיב והכא מודה בבעל מום מעיקרא דנפדה אע"ג דקדשי מזבח וממאי דתנא דמתני' סבירא ליה קדשי מזבח היו בכלל העמדה והערכה שצריכין שיהו חיין בשעת פדייה כדכתיב והעמיד את הבהמה לפני הכהן ואח"כ והעריך אותה מדקתני סיפא גבי קדם הקדשן את מומן דאגב שקידשן למזבח מקדישין תמימים:
notes.en: As we learned: Rabbi Shimon says, etc.: since Rabbi Shimon says that items consecrated for Temple maintenance were not included, by implication the verse is written about items consecrated for the altar; and here he concedes regarding one blemished from the outset that it is redeemed, even though it is consecrated for the altar. And from where do we know that the tanna of our mishna holds that items consecrated for the altar were included in standing and valuation, which require that they be alive at the time of redemption, as it is written, “Then he shall stand the animal before the priest,” and afterward, “and the priest shall appraise it”? From what it teaches in the latter clause about animals whose consecration preceded their blemish [that they must be buried], since when he consecrated them for the altar he consecrated them unblemished.

messages.text: And Rabbi Shimon concedes with regard to an animal that was blemished from the outset, i.e., before it was consecrated, that it may be redeemed even if it was consecrated for the altar.

notes.he: למאי דאמרינן בסמוך דרב סבר כר"ל [דאמר התם] לרבנן קדשי מזבח לא היו בכלל העמדה והערכה ניחא דמודה לרבנן אבל למאי דמסקינן דסבר כר' יוחנן דלרבנן אחד זה ואחד זה היו בכלל העמדה והערכה אם כן מודה למאן ויש לפרש דנקט הכי דלא תיסק אדעתא טעמא דמתניתין משום דאין פודין לאכילה לכלבים ולא משום העמדה והערכה דלא בעינן בקדשי מזבח העמדה והערכה ולכך ברישא דקדם מומן יפדו והשתא קמ"ל דטעמא דמתני' משום העמדה והערכה וכדדייקינן בסמוך מדלא קתני ואם נעשו טריפה וברישא דקדם מומן מודה רבי שמעון דלא בעי העמדה והערכה והשתא דנקט מודה רבי שמעון משום דאיכא למיטעי דפליג אמתני' כדפרישית איצטריך למימר דשפיר מודה בה והא דנקט רבי שמעון משום דלדידיה פשיטא ליה טפי דקדשי מזבח היו בכלל העמדה והערכה מדקאמר קדשי בדק הבית לא היו ע"כ כי כתיבא העמדה והערכה בקדשי מזבח כתיבא אבל לרבנן לא פשיטא ליה כולי האי דמצי למימר לא היו כמו שאומר ריש לקיש:
notes.en: In brief: And Rabbi Shimon concedes regarding one blemished from the outset. According to what is said shortly (15a), that Rav holds like Reish Lakish, who says that according to the Rabbis items consecrated for the altar were not included in standing and valuation, it is well that Rabbi Shimon “concedes” to the Rabbis. But according to the conclusion that Rav holds like Rabbi Yoḥanan, that according to the Rabbis both kinds were included, to whom does he concede? One may explain that it says this so that you should not think the reason of our mishna is that one does not redeem in order to feed dogs, and not standing and valuation, as though items for the altar did not need standing and valuation, which is why in the first clause, where the blemish came first, they are redeemed. It teaches us that the reason of the mishna is standing and valuation, as the Gemara soon infers from the fact that it does not teach “and if they became tereifa”; and in the first clause, where the blemish came first, Rabbi Shimon concedes that standing and valuation are not required. Since one might err and think he disagrees with the mishna, it had to say that he concedes it. And it names Rabbi Shimon because for him it is more obvious that items for the altar were included in standing and valuation: since he says items for Temple maintenance were not, the verse must be speaking of items for the altar. For the Rabbis it is not so obvious, since one could say they were not included, as Reish Lakish says. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: קודם הקדש דאע"ג דקדשי מזבח בעו העמדה והערכה האי בעל מום מעיקרא לא חל עליהם הקדש גמור למזבח הלכך אפי' מתו דלא מצי למעבד בהו העמדה יפדו דקדושת דמים הוא ודינו כקדשי בדק הבית דלא היו בכלל העמדה והערכה:
notes.en: And Rabbi Shimon concedes regarding one blemished from the outset: before consecration. For even though items consecrated for the altar require standing and valuation, on this one, blemished from the outset, full consecration for the altar did not take effect. Therefore, even if they died, when one cannot stand them, they are redeemed, for it is sanctity of value and its law is like that of items consecrated for Temple maintenance, which were not included in standing and valuation.

messages.text: What is the reason? It is derived from a verse, as the verse states: “Then he shall stand the animal before the priest. And the priest shall appraise it”. The emphasis on “it” serves to exclude an animal that was blemished from the outset.

verse.he: וְהֶעֱרִיךְ הַכֹּהֵן אֹתָהּ בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע כְּעֶרְכְּךָ הַכֹּהֵן כֵּן יִהְיֶה׃
verse.en: and the priest shall assess it. Whether high or low, whatever assessment is set by the priest shall stand;

notes.he: כל קדשי בדק הבית לרבי שמעון ממעטינן מקרא אחרינא בסוף תמורה (דף לג.):
notes.en: “It,” to exclude one blemished from the outset: all items consecrated for Temple maintenance, according to Rabbi Shimon, we exclude from another verse, at the end of Temura (33a).

messages.text: With regard to both animals consecrated for the altar and animals consecrated for Temple maintenance, if they died they must be buried.

notes.he: אפי' בעל מום מעיקרא דסברי דהכל היו בכלל העמדה והערכה והלכך כיון דמתו דלא מצי למעבד להו העמדה משום דלאו בר פדיה נינהו אלא יקברו. והני חכמים לאו בר פלוגתיה דר' שמעון דפליגי עליה בתמורה נינהו אלא שאר חכמים תנא דבי לוי נינהו דמחמיר בבעל מום מעיקרו:
notes.en: And the Rabbis say: if they died they must be buried: even one blemished from the outset, for they hold that all were included in standing and valuation. Therefore, since they died and one cannot stand them, they are not subject to redemption; rather, they must be buried. And these Rabbis are not Rabbi Shimon’s disputants who disagree with him in Temura, but other Rabbis: the tanna of the school of Levi, who is stringent regarding one blemished from the outset.

messages.text: Whose opinion is that of the Rabbis in the mishna? It is the opinion of the tanna of the school of Levi, as the school of Levi taught:
messages.quote: if they died they must be buried

notes.he: לאו הנך רבנן דפליגי עליה דר' שמעון במס' תמורה דהתם אמרינן לדברי הכל בעל מום מעיקרו לא היה בכלל העמדה והערכה אלא תנא דבי לוי הוא:
notes.en: But the Rabbis: not those Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Shimon in Tractate Temura, for there we say that according to all, one blemished from the outset was not included in standing and valuation. Rather, it is the tanna of the school of Levi.

messages.text: All animals were included in the obligation of standing and valuation, even an animal that was blemished from the outset.
And similarly, the school of Levi taught in Levi’s own collection of baraitot:
Even an undomesticated animal and even a bird are included in the obligation of standing and valuation, despite the fact that they can never be sacrificed upon the altar.

notes.he: דאינה ראויה למזבח:
notes.en: Even an undomesticated animal: which is not fit for the altar.

messages.text: But isn’t it written: “And the priest shall appraise it,” which is an expression of exclusion? If so, the verse must be excluding some case, at least that of an undomesticated animal or a bird. The phrase “and the priest shall appraise it” is difficult according to the opinion of the tanna of the school of Levi.

notes.he: כלומר דאותה בעי העמדה והערכה למעוטי בעל מום מעיקרו שמתו דאע"ג דאינו בר העמדה נפדה קשיא:
notes.en: But isn’t it written “it”? That is to say: “it” requires standing and valuation, which excludes one blemished from the outset that died, which is redeemed even though it cannot stand. It is difficult.

messages.text: But in light of this difficulty, according to the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Shimon in the mishna in Temura, what is the halakha? Is it indeed so that if animals whose blemish preceded their consecration died they may be redeemed, as derived from the word “it”? If that is so, then why did Rav say: This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon?
messages.quote: This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon

notes.he: דבבעל מום מעיקרא מודו:
notes.en: So too, if they died they are redeemed: since they concede regarding one blemished from the outset.

notes.he: אבל רבנן דפליגי עליה דר' שמעון במסכת תמורה דאמרי אחד קדשי מזבח ואחד קדשי בדק הבית היו בכלל העמדה והערכה ומודין היו בבעלי מומין מעיקרו שמפדין הכי נמי דיפדו נמי לאחר מיתה:
notes.en: But the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Shimon in Tractate Temura, who say that both items consecrated for the altar and items consecrated for Temple maintenance were included in standing and valuation, and who concede that animals blemished from the outset are redeemed: so too would they be redeemed after death?

notes.he: נימא זו דברי רבי שמעון ומחלוקתו:
notes.en: If so: let him say: This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon and those who disagree with him.

messages.text: Continued on 15a: if the Rabbis agree, Rav should have said “This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon and those who disagree with him.”
